text:
Connor Bedard isn't hiding behind the rebuild. "WE all said we think we're going to win this year. WE set the expectations on ourselves," he said, in a post from The Athletic's Mark Lazerus. The trouble is the standings. The Blackhawks are 0-4-1 in their last five, outscored 23-11, and the chances back it up: 37% of the expected goals in those games. Nine points in 17 games leaves our playoff simulations giving them about a 0.3% chance.

Saturday's stop is about the worst one available. Carolina is 4-1-0 in its last five and owns 58% of the five-on-five expected goals this season. Pyotr Kochetkov is on a heater (.945 and 6.9 goals saved above expected over his last five starts), and with Jordan Staal out with a calf injury, Jackson Blake has slid in beside Martinook and Ehlers and kept his point streak going to eight games. Logan Stankoven has 12 points in 10, and he's earning them. Our numbers expect 3.87 goals for the Hurricanes and 2.44 for Chicago.

If you're a Hawks fan looking for a reason to watch, it's Roman Kantserov. He has points in seven straight and goals in three straight, and he's put words to the adjustment: "In the first games, I was confused, like, 'Wow, it's so fast.' But now I just feel I'm at this speed and it's good for me" (via Lazerus). He scored 36 goals in 63 KHL games for Magnitogorsk last season, so this isn't coming from nowhere. With Patrick Kane out, Anton Frondell has moved onto the top power play and is up to 18:41 a night.

One Carolina name to keep an eye on: Mark Jankowski, our depth sleeper. He's on the third line, but his 4.4 expected goals over his last ten games rate better than 99% of depth forwards. We have him at 25% to score.
headline: Chicago's one bright spot walks into Raleigh

hunch.text: Kantserov keeps the one good thing in Chicago going and scores in a fourth straight game, even if the night goes the way our numbers expect.
